note: Plain-language phrases for each dimension band, used to describe a book in relation to the profile. Editable like the rest of profile/ — nothing here is compiled into code.

D1.dual_timeline: runs a historical rupture straight into the present
D1.period_causal: period-set, with the causal line running forward
D1.generational: a multi-generational sweep over one family or one place
D1.aftermath: contemporary, but built as the aftermath of something specific
D1.texture_only: historical texture with no argument behind it

D2.land: driven by land, water, extraction or labour
D2.state_violence: driven by state violence, conquest or repression
D2.institution: about how an institution forms the people inside it
D2.domestic: family, marriage and identity as the engine
D2.media_tech: contemporary media and internet life as the subject

D3.alt_archive: an invented archive or an alternate history
D3.device_twist: a formal device that resolves into a reveal

D4.quippy: wry and comic at sentence level
D4.flat: prose the review names as the weak point

high: Close to the centre of the profile.
This is the shape the profile keeps acquiring.
good: This one holds up against the profile.
Enough of the profile is here.
near: Half of what the profile wants.
some: The subject is closer than the book.
off: Not what the profile goes for.

connectors.anchor: Nearest thing in your own set is
connectors.noAnchor: Nothing in your set sits especially close.
connectors.thin: The review is short enough that several dimensions fell back to defaults, so read this as a guess.
